name: GemPages
summary: Shopify page and sales-funnel builder with a drag-and-drop editor, prebuilt templates, post-purchase upsells and A/B offer testing.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want a drag-and-drop page and funnel builder with upsells and A/B offer testing
skip_if: you are not on Shopify, or you only need a few basic pages and cannot justify a monthly app fee
honest_knock: The tiers gate what most stores want: the free plan allows 1 published page, Build caps theme sections at 20 and limits post-purchase upsell volume, and Optimize is needed for unlimited upsell volume, 100 theme sections, headless instant landing pages and scheduled publishing. The pricing page also mentions paying commission as you grow, and we could not find how that is calculated, so ask before you commit at scale. Publishing failed once in our test until the Theme Helper was switched on.

Optimize: $59/mo, or $47/mo billed yearly at $564/yr (save $144). Enterprise: $199/mo, or $159/mo billed yearly at $1,908/yr (save $480), sold via a contact-us call. Inside the app on 19 November 2026 the paid plans showed 20% off for the first 3 months (Build $23.2, Optimize $47.2, Enterprise $159.2 a month). The pricing page does not say whether Shopify's own plan or other fees apply, and the higher plans mention paying commission as you grow.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 19 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, with the app on the free plan and the interface in English. We installed GemPages, picked a prebuilt landing page template, changed its heading, added a product and published the page. We did not pay for anything.
findings: Install: no payment screen appeared. The app opened on a Welcome page on the free plan, about 30 seconds after the click on Install.
Editing: a prebuilt landing page template loaded in the editor and we changed its heading and added a product element within about a minute.
Publishing: the first publish failed with 'GemPages Theme Helper is off'. After we switched it on, the page published about 2 minutes 15 seconds after the click on Install.
Free plan limit: after one published page the app showed 'You've reached the maximum number of published pages on your plan (1/1)' with an upgrade prompt.
Plans in the app: Free $0, Build $23.2, Optimize $47.2 and Enterprise $159.2 a month, each marked 20% off for the first 3 months. The App Store listing shows $29, $59 and $199 without that discount.
not_tested: the published page as a shopper sees it, because the test store is password protected

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?

Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: The pricing page does not say whether Shopify's own plan or other fees apply, and the higher plans mention paying commission as you grow; neither is calculated. Can you publish the price or the rule?
